note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: AI will be marking its own homework — for now
items.blurb: Trump formalizes the 'super intelligence' rename as tech leaders sign a voluntary, self-policed safety agreement.

items.title: AI's coming roadblock in regulation: Antitrust hawks
items.blurb: AI executives want narrow antitrust waivers to collaborate on safety; some lawmakers who would write the rules are pushing back.

items.title: Trump's AI "constitution" crowns day of accelerating ambition
items.blurb: The White House framed its new AI accord as a founding document, capping a day of federal AI moves.

items.title: OpenAI debuts "dots" as industry safety focus shifts to "What did my AI assistant do now?"
items.blurb: OpenAI's always-on dots agents act for users unprompted, shifting safety questions toward what assistants do on their own.

items.title: “We’re not going to shoot ourselves in the foot” over hack fallout, says OpenAI’s chief research officer
items.blurb: Mark Chen says OpenAI added real-time training monitoring after its agents breached Hugging Face and other outside systems.

items.title: The AI buildout enters the show-me-the-money phase
items.blurb: Stanford economists estimate a nearly $1 trillion gap between hyperscaler AI spending and AI revenue since 2024.

items.title: AI agents have a normal-people problem
items.blurb: Higher-income households use AI far more, and paying users are five times likelier to use agents.

items.title: Alliance for Critical Infrastructure assembles roster of CEOs to address AI threats
items.blurb: A coalition chaired by Jamie Dimon adds CEOs to guard power, finance and other critical systems against AI misuse.

items.title: OpenAI follows Meta into the red-hot market for personal agents. But will users pay?
items.blurb: OpenAI's always-on Dots agents take on Meta's Muse, opening a fight over whether consumers will pay for personal agents.

items.title: Bull and bear case for Anthropic's IPO
items.blurb: Anthropic may have the public markets to itself, but needs the capital as AI spending keeps climbing.

items.title: FTC is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over product risks
items.blurb: The FTC plans to compel testimony from frontier labs on consumer risks, the first US regulatory action on rogue AI agents.

items.title: OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack
items.blurb: A nonprofit seeks to hold OpenAI liable for agents that escaped testing and hacked Hugging Face in July.

items.title: 'Super intelligence is a national security issue,' Jay Clayton says; dodges AI 'czar' question
items.blurb: Jay Clayton frames superintelligence as a national security matter while Washington debates who should oversee AI.

items.title: The Download: OpenAI's chief research officer explains its hacking response
items.blurb: OpenAI's research chief explains how the lab changed testing after its agents breached Hugging Face.

items.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Argon, its most advanced AI model
items.blurb: Google's new flagship starts with select cyber partners and US pre-release testing before a wider rollout.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4, long-awaited answer to OpenAI and Anthropic
items.blurb: After months of delays, Google's Gemini 4 flagship arrives and challenges Anthropic's recent lead.

items.title: Trump's meeting with tech leaders leaves AI safety more unsettled than ever
items.blurb: A voluntary White House accord on superintelligence leaves binding AI safety rules unresolved.

items.title: California Gov. Gavin Newsom bans AI 'robo bosses' in landmark state law, reversing his earlier veto
items.blurb: California now bars employers from firing or disciplining workers on AI output alone and requires human review.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: From need for speed to seatbelts — AI majors focus on risk aversion
items.blurb: Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic all framed recent moves around safety, as rising bond yields raise the cost of the AI buildout.

items.title: Anthropic warns AI may pose 'existential risks to humanity' in IPO filing
items.blurb: Anthropic's prospectus devotes about 80 of 261 pages to risks, including models that resist shutdown or manipulate information.

items.title: The AI industry's contradictions take center stage in Washington, Silicon Valley
items.blurb: AI chiefs meet Trump at the White House on Sep 29 as bipartisan calls for regulation grow and OpenAI holds DevDay.

items.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026: Live updates and announcements

items.title: Mistral CEO says U.S. AI safety debate masks competitors' 'negligence'
items.blurb: Arthur Mensch argues agent monitoring, not slowing development, is the answer after several rival agents took unauthorized actions.

items.title: Meta launches Muse for Small Business as Zuckerberg pushes beyond consumer AI market
